column1: # Async dependency scoreboards beyond the six numbered SB0..SB5 -- the warp-state
# barriers the warpgroup-MMA / tensor-MMA / cluster path uses on Hopper and
# Blackwell.  These are NOT the SB0..SB5 control-word scoreboards; they are named
# warp-state resources the scheduler tracks as separate dependency barriers, and
# the producer->reader latency is a fixed model constant (the dependent reader is
# held that many cycles after the writer before the async result is visible).
# Recovered from binary analysis of CUDA-13.1 ptxas + nvdisasm: the SASS opcodes
# below are exactly what `ptxas -arch <sm>` emits and what `nvdisasm -c`
# disassembles on this toolchain.  sm_89 has none of these (no wgmma / tcgen05 /
# cluster), so this table is STATIC + documented; the SASS-opcode column is
# binary-confirmed on sm_90a (WARPGROUP/HGMMA/gsb0/UCGABAR) and sm_100a/sm_120a
# (UCGABAR cluster barrier).
# Columns:
#   scoreboard   the named warp-state barrier resource
#   readers      SASS ops that WAIT on / read the barrier (held until satisfied)
#   writers      SASS ops that ARM / advance the barrier
#   latency      writer->reader hold (cycles), fixed model constant
#   arch         architectures that have the resource (binary-confirmed emit)
#   note
scoreboard
WGMMA_ACCUM_SB
column6: warpgroup-MMA accumulator barrier: WARPGROUP.ARRIVE arms it, the async wgmma reads it; the next wgmma/WAIT/EXIT/special-reg read is held 6 cyc. Confirmed: ptxas emits WARPGROUP.ARRIVE -> HGMMA gsb0 on sm_90a.

column1: WGMMA_GROUP_SB
column6: the wgmma GROUP commit/wait barrier (gsb0 group id): each grouped wgmma advances it, WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE gsb0,N waits for <=N outstanding groups; reader hold 3 cyc. Confirmed: ptxas emits WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE gsb0,0x0 on sm_90a.

column1: CGA_BARRIER
column6: cluster (CGA) barrier warp-state: UCGABAR_ARV/SET arms, UCGABAR_WAIT/GET reads; reader hold 6 cyc; EXIT is an implicit reader (must drain cluster arrivals). Confirmed: ptxas emits CGAERRBAR/UCGABAR_ARV/UCGABAR_WAIT on sm_90a, sm_100a and sm_120a.

column1: WGMMA_ACCUM_SB
column6: datacenter Blackwell retains the warpgroup-MMA barrier resource (same 6-cyc model) alongside the tcgen05 path; the encoder retargets the MMA-issue opcode (tcgen05 UTCxMMA) but the async-barrier resource and latency are invariant.

column1: WGMMA_GROUP_SB
column6: Blackwell MMA-group commit/wait barrier (same 3-cyc group hold as Hopper); the grouped tensor-MMA advances it, DEPBAR waits the outstanding-group count.

column1: TCGEN05_TMEM
column6: tensor-memory (TMEM) producer->reader is scoreboard-tracked like a load (latency-1 decoupled, reader waits the SB), not a fixed-latency math result; LDTM/STTM and the UTCxMMA ops drive it. The TMEM result barrier is the Blackwell analogue of the wgmma accumulator wait.

column1: RPC
column6: implicit return-PC ordering resource: every branch/return op writes the RPC, following math is ordered 9 cyc behind it. Same RPC resource as the sm_89 RPC-ORDER rows in uniform_pred_hazards.tsv; listed here as a warp-state barrier for the newer arches that share it.

column1: RPC
column6: USETMAXREG (warp register reallocation) orders against following math at 8 cyc on the RPC resource -- one less than the branch writers; it must commit the new register window before dependent math issues.
